content.title: About
content.content: Hummus is a traditional Middle Eastern dip made from cooked chickpeas, tahini, olive oil, lemon juice, and spices. It has a creamy texture, a mild nutty flavor with a hint of acidity.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Hummus has been known in the Arab world for over 700 years.
The word “hummus” comes from Arabic “ḥummuṣ,” meaning “chickpea.”
Tahini (sesame paste) gives hummus its distinctive aroma and boosts its nutritional value.
In the United States, hummus gained popularity in the 1990s and became one of the top-selling vegetarian products by 2020.
There are many variations: roasted red pepper, garlic, olive, avocado, and more.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Chickpeas provide about 8 g of protein per 100 g, making hummus a good protein source for vegetarians.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Dietary fiber supports digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Healthy fats
items.content: Olive oil and tahini supply monounsaturated fats that are heart‑friendly.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: Hummus contains folate, iron, magnesium, phosphorus, and vitamin B6.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Chickpeas have a moderate glycemic index, helping to stabilize blood sugar levels.

items.title: Chickpea allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to legumes, including chickpeas.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Prepared hummus often contains added salt; those monitoring sodium intake should choose low‑salt versions.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Lemon juice can aggravate heartburn in people with high stomach acidity.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve hummus as a dip with vegetable sticks, pita bread, or crackers; use it in sandwiches, wraps, and salads. It can also be blended into sauces or used as a base for vegetarian dishes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep hummus in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 5 days. After opening, cover the surface with plastic wrap to prevent oxidation. Discard if it develops an off smell or discoloration.
